name: UPSC CSE Prelims
fullName: Union Public Service Commission – Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination
approxCandidates: ≈9–13 lakh applicants and ≈5–6 lakh appearing each year (recent cycles); 13,343 qualified for Mains 2026
eligibility: Graduate in any discipline; 21–32 yrs for General category (relaxations for reserved categories); attempt limits apply

notification.summary: CSE 2026: Prelims were held on 24 May 2026, the result came out on 15 June 2026 (13,343 qualified) and Mains began on 21 August 2026. Per UPSC's Calendar 2027 (released May 2026), the CSE 2027 notification is due on 13 January 2027 and Prelims on 23 May 2027. All dates are provisional, and upsc.gov.in itself could not be reached from the research sandbox.

pattern.notes: This mock covers GS Paper I only. GS Paper II (CSAT: 80 questions, 200 marks, 2 hours) is qualifying at 33% and is not simulated. A wrong answer costs one-third of the question's marks (0.66). The Mains cut-off is decided on GS Paper I marks alone. The question bank holds 60 items; the full paper has 100.

trendAnalysis.summary: Since 2023 the paper has leaned heavily on statement-based items ('how many of the above are correct', pairs, assertion–reason), which reward precise knowledge and make elimination harder. Polity (about 14–16 questions) and Economy (about 13–16) are the steady core. Environment, which peaked earlier in the decade, settled to about 9–12 in 2025–26. Science & Technology and International Relations/organisations have risen, with S&T at about 15–18 in 2026 by coaching-institute counts. History plus Art & Culture still yields about 20 questions, with growing culture coverage. Difficulty has stayed moderate-to-hard, with many current-affairs-linked static questions, and coaching tallies differ slightly by how each counts subjects.

resources.notes: UPSC posts question papers on upsc.gov.in under Examinations → Previous Question Papers soon after the exam. Official answer keys and cut-offs come out only after the whole CSE cycle ends with the final result.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the published GS Paper I question papers (UPSC posts them after the exam) and from post-exam subject-wise analyses by coaching institutes (VisionIAS, IASGyan, NextIAS) for 2024 and 2025, which report about 60–67% multi-statement items, a steady stream of 'Statement-I/Statement-II' items and 'how many pairs are correctly matched' items. The 2026 paper is covered from memory-based analyses and the writer's own knowledge, because the full text of those pages could not be fetched (WebSearch gave only summaries). Archetypes describe the recurring formats in our own words; no real question is reproduced.

archetypes.pattern: Constitutional/statutory office (CAG, Finance Commission, Election Commission, Attorney General): 3 statements on appointment, tenure, removal and post-retirement bars; 'how many are correct'. Trap: one statement swaps a statutory rule for a constitutional one.
Parliamentary procedure (Money Bills, joint sitting, no-confidence motion, Speaker's role) as numbered statements; trap is a plausible but wrong procedural detail.
Classify provisions (Fundamental Rights vs DPSP vs Fundamental Duties, Schedules, anti-defection) and pick the right code from a list of 3–4 items.
Landmark Supreme Court judgments and doctrines (basic structure, Art 21 expansion, Art 356 review, reservation limits): statements pairing case with holding.
Powers of President/Governor (ordinance, pardon, discretion) in the Statement-I/Statement-II format; trap: Statement-II is false or does not explain I.
Local government and federal provisions (73rd/74th Amendments, District Planning Committee, State Election Commission, Fifth/Sixth Schedule): 'how many correct'.
Count or select which listed bodies are constitutional (vs statutory/executive), e.g. NCSC, NCBC, GST Council, NHRC, CVC, NITI Aayog.
RBI monetary tools (repo, CRR, SLR, OMO, MPC) and their effects on liquidity and money supply; statements or Statement-I/II; trap reverses the direction of an effect.
Budget and fiscal terms (fiscal/primary/revenue deficit, capital vs revenue receipts, disinvestment): definition item or 'select the capital receipts' code.
National income and price indices (GDP, GNP, NDP, GVA, CPI vs WPI, NSO/Office of Economic Adviser): statements with one definitional twist.
Banking and financial instruments/institutions (T-bills, payments and small finance banks, PSL, bonds, NBFCs): 'how many correct'.
External sector: which items go to current vs capital account of BoP, ECB/FDI/FPI, exchange-rate effects; statement or Statement-I/II format.
Agricultural economy and pricing (MSP, CACP, FRP for sugarcane, procurement): statements on institutional status and legal basis.
International environmental conventions and protocols (Ramsar, CITES, CMS, Montreal/Kigali, Kyoto, Paris): statements on scope, legal nature and India's role.
Protected areas and species (national parks to states, endemic species, IUCN/WPA status, UNESCO MAB): pairs 'how many correctly matched' or single pick.
Core ecology concepts (food chains/pyramids, succession, eutrophication, nitrogen fixation): statements testing a common misconception.
Climate and pollution science (greenhouse gases, GWP, aerosols, black carbon, carbon capture): 'how many of the above' with 4 items.
Ecosystem processes (mangroves, wetlands, coral reefs) in Statement-I/Statement-II format.
Ancient sites, inscriptions and rulers matched as pairs (Harappan sites, prashastis, rock edicts): 'how many pairs correctly matched'.
Buddhism/Jainism and philosophical schools: councils, doctrines, language of preaching; statements.
Medieval administration, terms and literature (iqta, mansab, amara-nayaka, Vijayanagara and Sultanate facts): definition item or statements.
INC sessions, presidents and resolutions (Lahore, Karachi, Calcutta 1917, etc.): single pick or statements.
Colonial Acts and policies (Charter Acts, 1909/1919/1935 Acts, land revenue systems, Governors-General): statements or pairs.
Movements, organisations and personalities (Non-Cooperation, Quit India, reform societies and founders): pairs or Statement-I/II.
Performing and visual art forms matched to states/regions (dances, paintings, crafts): 'how many pairs correctly matched'.
Temple, cave and sculptural traditions (Nagara/Dravida/Vesara, Ajanta–Ellora, Gandhara/Mathura/Amaravati schools): statements.
Bhakti and Sufi traditions: saints, orders, practices and regions; statements with code options.
Indian rivers and drainage (west/east flowing, tributaries of a basin): select the right code.
Climatology (monsoon mechanism, western disturbances, orographic rain, atmosphere layers): statements or Statement-I/II.
World map items: seas/straits and bordering countries ('how many of these countries border X').
Soils, minerals and crops of India: properties statements (black/laterite/alluvial soils).
Physical geography processes (ocean currents, cyclones, El Niño/La Niña): statements or single pick.
Location facts of India (Tropic of Cancer states, international borders, mountain passes): 'which one is NOT' single pick.
Biotechnology and health (vaccines, CRISPR, monoclonal antibodies, GM crops, antimicrobial resistance): statements or Statement-I/II.
Space technology (orbits, launch vehicles, ISRO/NASA missions, Lagrange points): 'how many correct'.
Energy and emerging technology (nuclear programme, hydrogen types, quantum computing, LEDs, batteries): statements.
Applied everyday physics/chemistry (optics, materials, household phenomena): single-answer item.
International organisations: membership, HQ, functions and status (UNSC, WTO, IAEA, G20): statements or Statement-I/II.
Membership of groupings (SCO, Quad, BIMSTEC, BRICS, IORA): 'how many of these countries are members' or 'which is NOT a member'.
International financial institutions (IMF/SDR, World Bank, AIIB, NDB): shareholding, HQ, membership statements.
Flagship government schemes (nodal ministry, eligibility, funding pattern, targets): 'how many correct'.
Reports and indices matched to publishing organisations: pairs or single pick.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission of India:
1. It is constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution every fifth year or earlier.
2. Its recommendations on the distribution of tax proceeds are binding on the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission constituted by the President every five years or earlier. Its recommendations are advisory; the Union Government is not constitutionally bound to accept them. Hence only 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Which of the following are listed as Fundamental Duties under Article 51A of the Constitution of India?
1. To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
2. To vote in elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
3. To protect and improve the natural environment
4. To pay taxes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Safeguarding public property (51A(i)) and protecting the natural environment (51A(g)) are Fundamental Duties. Voting and paying taxes are not listed in Article 51A.

questions.question:
With reference to Money Bills, consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha can withhold a Money Bill for a maximum period of fourteen days.
2. The decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.
3. A Money Bill can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 109 limits the Rajya Sabha to 14 days; Article 110(3) makes the Speaker's decision final. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (Article 109(1)), so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 'basic structure' doctrine was first propounded by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case.
2. In the Minerva Mills case, the Supreme Court held that the limited nature of Parliament's amending power is itself a basic feature of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) laid down the basic structure doctrine. Minerva Mills (1980) struck down parts of the 42nd Amendment, holding that limited amending power is a basic feature. Both are correct.

questions.question:
Which of the following are constitutional bodies?
1. Election Commission of India
2. NITI Aayog
3. National Human Rights Commission
4. Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The Election Commission (Art. 324) and CAG (Art. 148) are constitutional bodies. NHRC is statutory (Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993) and NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution (2015).

questions.question:
With reference to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, consider the following statements:
1. Not less than one-third of the seats in Panchayats are reserved for women.
2. Elections to Panchayats are conducted by the State Election Commission.
3. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects that may be devolved to Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 243D reserves not less than one-third seats for women; Article 243K vests elections in the State Election Commission; the Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects. All three are correct.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the pardoning power:
1. The President can grant pardon to a person sentenced by a court martial, whereas the Governor of a State cannot.
2. The President exercises the pardoning power under Article 72 on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 72(1)(a) covers court-martial sentences, which Article 161 does not give the Governor. The Supreme Court (Maru Ram, 1980; Kehar Singh, 1989) held that the President acts on ministerial advice. Both are correct.

questions.question:
With reference to the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law), consider the following statements:
1. It was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
2. A member is not disqualified if the original party merges with another party and at least two-thirds of the members of the legislature party agree to the merger.
3. A 'split' involving one-third of the members of the legislature party continues to be a valid ground for exemption from disqualification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment (1985). Paragraph 4 protects mergers backed by two-thirds of the legislature party. The one-third 'split' exemption was deleted by the 91st Amendment (2003), so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Attorney General of India:
1. He/she is appointed by the President and must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. He/she has the right to speak in either House of Parliament but not the right to vote.
3. He/she is a member of the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 76 sets the appointment and qualification. Article 88 lets the AG speak in Parliament without a vote. The AG is not a member of the Union Cabinet, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
If the Reserve Bank of India raises the policy repo rate, which of the following is/are likely?
1. The cost of borrowing from the RBI for commercial banks increases.
2. The step is generally aimed at containing inflation.
3. The Cash Reserve Ratio rises automatically.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The repo rate is what banks pay to borrow from the RBI, so a hike makes that borrowing dearer and tightens money supply to curb inflation. The CRR is a separate instrument and does not change automatically.

questions.question: In Union Budget terminology, Fiscal Deficit is equal to:
options: Total expenditure minus (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts)
Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + recoveries of loans + other non-debt receipts such as disinvestment). It measures the government's total borrowing requirement. Option C is the revenue deficit and option D is the effective revenue deficit.

questions.question: In India's national accounts, 'Gross Value Added at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies' gives:
questions.explanation: Since the 2011-12 base revision, GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies.

questions.question:
With reference to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) norms of the RBI, consider the following statements:
1. Agriculture is one of the categories under priority sector.
2. PSL targets apply only to public sector banks.
3. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises are included in the priority sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Agriculture and MSMEs are PSL categories. PSL targets also apply to private sector banks, foreign banks (with prescribed thresholds), small finance banks and others, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The inflation target under India's flexible inflation targeting framework is set in terms of the Consumer Price Index (Combined).
2. The Wholesale Price Index is compiled and released by the National Statistics Office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The target (4% ± 2%) is defined on headline CPI-Combined, which the NSO (MoSPI) compiles. The WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce & Industry), not the NSO.

questions.question:
Which of the following are recorded in the current account of India's Balance of Payments?
1. Remittances sent home by Indians working abroad
2. Foreign Direct Investment inflows
3. Exports of software services
4. External Commercial Borrowings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Private transfers (remittances) and services trade are current account items. FDI and ECBs are capital/financial account flows.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):
1. It is constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (as amended).
2. It has six members, three of whom are from the RBI including the Governor.
3. In case of a tie, the Governor has a second or casting vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Section 45ZB of the RBI Act (inserted in 2016) creates a six-member MPC: three RBI members including the Governor, who chairs it, and three external members. The Governor has a casting vote when votes are tied. All three statements are correct.

questions.question:
With reference to Treasury Bills in India, consider the following statements:
1. They are issued by the Government of India through the RBI.
2. They are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value.
3. They have a maturity of more than one year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: T-Bills are short-term money market instruments (91, 182 and 364 days) issued by the Central Government through the RBI at a discount. Their maturity is less than one year, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question: In government accounts, proceeds from disinvestment of the government's equity in public sector enterprises are classified as:
questions.explanation: Disinvestment reduces the government's assets and creates no liability, so it is a non-debt capital receipt.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands is a treaty administered under the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
2. The Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar sites where changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is an intergovernmental treaty that is not part of the UN/UNEP system; it has its own secretariat in Gland, Switzerland. The Montreux Record is correctly described.

questions.question:
Which of the following greenhouse gases are covered under the Kyoto Protocol?
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Methane
3. Nitrous oxide
4. Sulphur hexafluoride
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The Kyoto basket covers CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, HFCs, PFCs and SF₆; NF₃ was added in the second commitment period. All four listed gases are included.

questions.question: Which was the first Indian biosphere reserve to be included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was the first Indian reserve added to the network, in 2000. Gulf of Mannar and Sundarbans followed in 2001 and Nanda Devi in 2004.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about eutrophication:
1. It is commonly caused by excessive inflow of nitrates and phosphates into water bodies.
2. It leads to an increase in dissolved oxygen in the deeper layers of the water body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms. When the algae die, decomposers consume oxygen, so dissolved oxygen falls (hypoxia) and does not rise. Only 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Which of the following organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen?
1. Rhizobium
2. Azotobacter
3. Anabaena
4. Penicillium
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Rhizobium (symbiotic), Azotobacter (free-living) and the cyanobacterium Anabaena fix nitrogen. Penicillium is a fungus and does not.

questions.question:
With reference to the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, consider the following statements:
1. It aims at phasing down the production and consumption of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).
2. HFCs are potent greenhouse gases with high global warming potential.
3. HFCs are among the most significant ozone-depleting substances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Kigali Amendment (2016) phases down HFCs because of their high global warming potential. HFCs contain no chlorine or bromine and have negligible ozone-depletion potential, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question: Which one of the following ecological pyramids can never be inverted?
options: None of the above; all can be inverted
questions.explanation: Energy is lost at every trophic transfer (roughly 10% passes on), so the pyramid of energy is always upright. Number and biomass pyramids can be inverted, for example in a tree ecosystem or in aquatic biomass.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about mangroves:
1. Mangroves grow in the intertidal zones of tropical and subtropical coastlines.
2. Pneumatophores help many mangrove species obtain oxygen in waterlogged, anaerobic soils.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Mangroves are salt-tolerant intertidal vegetation, and pneumatophores (aerial roots) allow gas exchange in oxygen-poor mud.

questions.question:
Which of the following categories of protected areas are provided for under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972?
1. National Parks
2. Conservation Reserves
3. Community Reserves
4. Biosphere Reserves
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Sanctuaries, National Parks, Conservation Reserves and Community Reserves (the last two added in 2003) are notified under the WPA. Biosphere Reserves come under a separate scheme linked to UNESCO's MAB programme, not the WPA.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Harappan site : feature):
1. Lothal : dockyard
2. Kalibangan : evidence of a ploughed field
3. Dholavira : located in present-day Punjab
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Lothal (Gujarat) has a dockyard and Kalibangan (Rajasthan) has a pre-Harappan ploughed field. Dholavira is in the Kachchh district of Gujarat, so pair 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Buddhist Councils:
1. The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra during the reign of Ashoka.
2. The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir during the reign of Kanishka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The Third Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa. The Fourth was held in Kashmir (Kundalvana) under Kanishka, presided over by Vasumitra.

questions.question: The Telugu work 'Amuktamalyada' was composed by which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya of the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu. Allasani Peddana was a poet at his court, not a ruler.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal mansabdari system:
1. 'Zat' indicated the personal rank and salary of a mansabdar, while 'sawar' indicated the number of horsemen he had to maintain.
2. Mansabs were hereditary and passed automatically to the mansabdar's sons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. Mansabs were not hereditary: a mansabdar's rank ended with his service or death, and his sons had to earn their own. Only 1 is correct.

questions.question: The resolution declaring 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) as the goal of the Indian National Congress was adopted at which session?
questions.explanation: The Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution. 26 January 1930 was then observed as Independence Day.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress (1931):
1. It adopted resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.
2. It was presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. Sardar Patel presided over the Karachi session (March 1931), which endorsed the Gandhi–Irwin Pact and adopted the Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy resolution.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (land revenue system : person associated):
1. Permanent Settlement : Lord Cornwallis
2. Ryotwari System : Thomas Munro
3. Mahalwari System : Holt Mackenzie
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All three pairs are correct. Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793), Munro (with Alexander Read) the Ryotwari system in Madras, and Holt Mackenzie (Regulation VII, 1822) the Mahalwari system.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy (brought in by the 1919 Act), introduced provincial autonomy and proposed dyarchy at the Centre. It also set up the Federal Court, which began functioning in 1937. Only 2 is correct.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Quit India Movement:
1. The Quit India resolution was passed at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee in August 1942.
2. Parallel governments were set up in places such as Ballia, Tamluk and Satara during the movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The AICC passed the resolution at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942, and parallel governments emerged at Ballia (UP), Tamluk (Bengal) and Satara (Maharashtra).

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (classical dance : state of origin):
1. Sattriya : Assam
2. Mohiniyattam : Kerala
3. Kuchipudi : Odisha
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Sattriya comes from Assam and Mohiniyattam from Kerala. Kuchipudi comes from Andhra Pradesh, while Odisha's classical dance is Odissi.

questions.question: 'Vimana' (the pyramidal tower over the sanctum) and elaborate 'gopurams' (gateway towers) are characteristic features of which style of temple architecture?
questions.explanation: Dravida-style temples of South India have a pyramidal vimana and, in later phases, towering gopurams. Nagara temples have a curvilinear shikhara.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ajanta caves are exclusively Buddhist.
2. The Ellora caves contain Buddhist, Hindu and Jain excavations.
3. The Kailasa temple at Ellora was excavated under the Rashtrakutas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. Ajanta is entirely Buddhist, Ellora has 34 caves of the three faiths, and the Kailasa temple (Cave 16) is attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Bhakti tradition:
1. The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu, while the Nayanars were devotees of Shiva.
2. Basavanna is associated with the Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement in Karnataka.
3. Kabir composed his verses mainly in classical Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Kabir composed in a vernacular (Sadhukkadi/Hindavi), not in classical Sanskrit.

questions.question:
Which of the following rivers flow westward and drain into the Arabian Sea?
1. Narmada
2. Tapi
3. Mahanadi
4. Sabarmati
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The Narmada, Tapi and Sabarmati are west-flowing rivers that drain into the Arabian Sea. The Mahanadi flows east into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Western Disturbances:
1. They originate over the Mediterranean region.
2. The winter precipitation they bring is beneficial for rabi crops in north-west India.
3. They are the main cause of rainfall during the retreating south-west monsoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances are extratropical cyclonic systems from the Mediterranean that bring winter rain and snow, which helps wheat and other rabi crops. They are not the cause of retreating-monsoon rainfall.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (strait : water bodies it connects):
1. Strait of Hormuz : Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
2. Bab-el-Mandeb : Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
3. Strait of Gibraltar : Black Sea and Mediterranean Sea
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean; the Black Sea joins the Mediterranean through the Bosporus and Dardanelles.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about black (regur) soils of India:
1. They are formed largely by the weathering of basaltic lava rocks of the Deccan.
2. They have a high moisture-retention capacity.
3. They are rich in nitrogen and phosphorus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Black soils derive from Deccan basalt, retain moisture well (they swell when wet and crack when dry) and are rich in lime, iron, magnesia and potash. They are generally poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter.

questions.question:
Which of the following are cold ocean currents?
1. Benguela Current
2. Kuroshio Current
3. Humboldt (Peru) Current
4. Agulhas Current
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The Benguela (off south-west Africa) and Humboldt (off Peru–Chile) currents are cold. The Kuroshio and Agulhas currents are warm.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies entirely south of it.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Earth's atmosphere:
1. The thickness of the troposphere is greatest over the equator.
2. Most of the atmospheric ozone is found in the stratosphere.
3. Temperature normally increases with height in the troposphere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The troposphere is about 18 km thick at the equator and about 8 km at the poles, and roughly 90% of ozone lies in the stratosphere. Temperature normally falls with height in the troposphere (about 6.5 °C per km), so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question: Which one of the following pairs (mountain pass : location) is NOT correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Zoji La links the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh on the Srinagar–Leh route and is not in Arunachal Pradesh. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about mRNA vaccines:
1. They deliver messenger RNA that instructs the body's cells to make an antigenic protein, which triggers an immune response.
2. They work by permanently altering the DNA of the recipient's cells.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: mRNA stays in the cytoplasm, is translated into the antigen and then degrades. It does not enter the nucleus or alter the recipient's DNA.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. A geostationary satellite orbits in the plane of the Earth's equator.
2. Geostationary orbit lies at an altitude of about 36,000 km above the equator.
3. Sun-synchronous polar orbits used for remote sensing lie at higher altitudes than the geostationary orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite sits about 35,786 km above the equator with a 24-hour period. Sun-synchronous orbits are low Earth orbits of roughly 600–900 km, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about CRISPR-Cas9:
1. It is derived from a naturally occurring adaptive immune mechanism in bacteria.
2. Cas9 is an enzyme that cuts DNA at a specific location guided by a guide RNA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. Bacteria use CRISPR sequences to remember viral DNA, and in genome editing a guide RNA directs the Cas9 nuclease to cut DNA at the target site.

questions.question: The third stage of India's three-stage nuclear power programme is based on:
options: Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors using natural uranium
Fast Breeder Reactors using plutonium-based fuel
questions.explanation: Stage I uses PHWRs on natural uranium and Stage II uses Fast Breeder Reactors to breed fissile material. Stage III aims to use India's large thorium reserves, with thorium converted to U-233 as the fuel.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Antibiotics are not effective against viral infections.
2. Misuse of antibiotics in human medicine and livestock contributes to antimicrobial resistance.
3. Penicillin was discovered by Louis Pasteur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses, and their misuse drives antimicrobial resistance. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs):
1. LEDs emit light through electroluminescence when electrons and holes recombine at a p-n junction.
2. Efficient blue LEDs, which made white LED lighting possible, are based on gallium nitride semiconductors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics recognised the invention of efficient GaN-based blue LEDs.

questions.question:
With reference to the Sun–Earth Lagrange point L1, consider the following statements:
1. L1 lies on the line joining the Sun and the Earth, about 1.5 million km from the Earth.
2. ISRO's Aditya-L1 solar observatory was placed in a halo orbit around L1.
3. A spacecraft at L1 remains permanently in the Earth's shadow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: L1 lies about 1.5 million km sunward of the Earth, and Aditya-L1 operates in a halo orbit around it. From L1 a spacecraft views the Sun continuously without eclipses, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank (NDB):
1. It was established by the BRICS countries.
2. Its headquarters is in Shanghai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The NDB was set up under the 2014 Fortaleza agreement by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa and is headquartered in Shanghai.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the UN Security Council:
1. Its non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.
2. A retiring non-permanent member is eligible for immediate re-election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 23 of the UN Charter provides two-year terms for the 10 non-permanent members and states that a retiring member is not eligible for immediate re-election.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the G20:
1. The G20 has a permanent secretariat headquartered in Geneva.
2. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 at the New Delhi Summit in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The G20 has no permanent secretariat; the rotating presidency, supported by a troika, runs it. The African Union joined as a permanent member at the September 2023 New Delhi Summit.

questions.question:
India is a member of which of the following groupings?
1. Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
2. Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad)
3. North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
4. Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: India is a member of the SCO (since 2017), the Quad and IORA. It is not a member of NATO.

questions.question: Which one of the following currencies is NOT part of the basket that determines the value of the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR)?
questions.explanation: The SDR basket has five currencies: the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling. The Swiss franc is not included.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG):
1. The CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
2. The CAG holds office for a term of six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
3. After ceasing to hold office, the CAG is eligible for further office under the Government of India.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is Article 148(1). Statement 2 is the tenure under the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 148(4) makes the CAG ineligible for further office under the Union or any State. So two are correct.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. The Constitution does not prescribe the qualifications of the members of the Election Commission.
2. The Constitution fixes the term of office of the Election Commissioners at six years.
3. Under the 2023 law on their appointment, the Chief Justice of India is a member of the Selection Committee that recommends the Chief Election Commissioner.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. Article 324 leaves tenure and conditions of service to law, so the six-year term comes from statute, not the Constitution. The 2023 Act's Selection Committee is the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister; the Chief Justice is not on it.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A Bill to amend the Constitution cannot be passed at a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.
Statement-II: Article 368 requires a Constitution Amendment Bill to be passed by each House separately by a special majority.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both are correct. Because Article 368 requires passage in each House separately by a special majority, a deadlock on an amendment Bill cannot be resolved by a joint sitting under Article 108. Statement-II is the reason for Statement-I.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.
2. A motion of no-confidence in the Council of Ministers needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted.
3. A motion of no-confidence can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. Article 118(4) makes the Speaker preside over a joint sitting. Under the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure, leave to move a no-confidence motion needs at least 50 members. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha only (Article 75(3)), so the motion lies only there.

questions.question:
Which of the following are Directive Principles of State Policy under the Constitution of India?
1. Securing a uniform civil code for citizens
2. Separation of the judiciary from the executive
3. Protection of monuments and places of national importance
4. Abolition of untouchability
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Items 1, 2 and 3 are Articles 44, 50 and 49 (Part IV). Abolition of untouchability is a Fundamental Right under Article 17 (Part III).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Indra Sawhney case, the Supreme Court upheld reservation for Other Backward Classes but excluded the 'creamy layer'.
2. In the S.R. Bommai case, the Supreme Court held that a proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review.
3. In the Maneka Gandhi case, the Supreme Court held that the procedure depriving a person of personal liberty must be just, fair and reasonable.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three correctly state the holdings: Indra Sawhney (1992) on OBC reservation and the creamy layer, S.R. Bommai (1994) on judicial review of President's Rule, and Maneka Gandhi (1978) reading 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 as fair, just and reasonable.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: An ordinance promulgated by the President ceases to operate at the expiry of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament, unless disapproved earlier.
Statement-II: The President can promulgate an ordinance only when both Houses of Parliament are in session.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I restates Article 123(2)(a). Statement-II is wrong: Article 123 allows an ordinance only when both Houses are NOT in session (or one is not in session).

questions.question:
With reference to the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, consider the following statements:
1. It added the Twelfth Schedule, which lists 18 functional items for municipalities.
2. It provides for a District Planning Committee to consolidate the plans prepared by panchayats and municipalities.
3. It requires each State to set up a separate election commission for municipalities, distinct from the one for panchayats.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Twelfth Schedule; Article 243ZD). Statement 3 is wrong: Article 243ZA vests municipal elections in the same State Election Commission referred to in Article 243K.

questions.question:
Consider the following bodies:
1. National Commission for Scheduled Castes
2. National Commission for Backward Classes
3. National Human Rights Commission
4. Central Vigilance Commission
5. Goods and Services Tax Council
How many of the above are constitutional bodies?
questions.explanation: NCSC (Article 338), NCBC (Article 338B, after the 102nd Amendment, 2018) and the GST Council (Article 279A) are constitutional. The NHRC (Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993) and the CVC (CVC Act, 2003) are statutory. So three.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Banks do not earn any interest from the RBI on the balances they keep to meet the Cash Reserve Ratio.
2. The Statutory Liquidity Ratio is maintained by banks as deposits with the RBI.
3. A reduction in the Cash Reserve Ratio lowers the money multiplier.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. SLR assets (cash, gold, approved securities) are held by the banks themselves, not deposited with the RBI. A CRR cut frees reserves and raises the money multiplier.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: When the RBI buys government securities through open market operations, liquidity in the banking system increases.
Statement-II: In an open market purchase, the RBI pays for the securities by crediting the reserve balances of banks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both are correct and II explains I: paying for the securities adds to banks' reserves with the RBI, which is an injection of liquidity.

questions.question:
Which of the following are capital receipts of the Government of India?
1. Recovery of loans given to States
2. Proceeds from disinvestment
3. Dividends received from public sector enterprises
4. Market borrowings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Loan recoveries, disinvestment and borrowings either create a liability or reduce an asset, so they are capital receipts. Dividends are non-tax revenue receipts.

questions.question: In government budgeting, 'primary deficit' is equal to:
options: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets
questions.explanation: Primary deficit removes interest payments on past debt from the fiscal deficit. Revenue deficit minus grants for capital assets is the effective revenue deficit.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross National Product equals Gross Domestic Product plus net factor income from abroad.
2. Net Domestic Product equals Gross Domestic Product minus depreciation.
3. If net factor income from abroad is negative, GNP is larger than GDP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are standard identities. If net factor income from abroad is negative, GNP = GDP + (a negative number), so GNP is smaller than GDP; statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
With reference to payments banks in India, consider the following statements:
1. They cannot issue credit cards.
2. They can issue debit cards.
3. They must invest at least 75% of their demand deposit balances in SLR-eligible Government securities or treasury bills.
4. They cannot undertake lending activities.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are features of the RBI's licensing guidelines for payments banks: no lending and no credit cards, debit cards allowed, and at least 75% of demand deposits parked in SLR-eligible government paper.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Fresh External Commercial Borrowings raised by Indian companies are recorded in the capital account of India's Balance of Payments.
Statement-II: Interest paid on such borrowings is also recorded in the capital account.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: The borrowing itself changes India's external liabilities, so it is a capital account item. Interest payments are investment income (primary income) in the current account, so Statement-II is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India announces Minimum Support Prices after considering the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
2. The CACP is a statutory body.
3. The Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane is fixed under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The CACP is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, not a statutory body.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. CITES is legally binding on its Parties, but it does not take the place of national laws.
2. The Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals is also known as the Bonn Convention.
3. India hosted the thirteenth Conference of the Parties (COP13) of the Convention on Migratory Species at Gandhinagar in 2020.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. CITES binds Parties, who implement it through their own laws. The CMS was signed at Bonn in 1979, and its COP13 was held at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, in February 2020.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Under the Paris Agreement, the emission-reduction targets in each country's Nationally Determined Contribution are set by that country itself.
Statement-II: The Paris Agreement requires Parties to communicate a new or updated Nationally Determined Contribution every five years.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both are true. Statement-I describes the bottom-up nature of NDCs; Statement-II describes the five-yearly update cycle. The update cycle does not explain why targets are self-determined.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (protected area : State):
1. Dachigam National Park : Jammu and Kashmir
2. Namdapha National Park : Arunachal Pradesh
3. Silent Valley National Park : Tamil Nadu
4. Bandhavgarh National Park : Madhya Pradesh
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley is in Palakkad district, Kerala. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.question: Which one of the following animals is endemic to the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The lion-tailed macaque is found only in the Western Ghats. The hoolock gibbon is found in north-east India, and the red panda and snow leopard in the Himalaya.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about ecological succession:
1. Primary succession begins in areas where no soil exists, such as bare rock.
2. Lichens are often pioneer species on bare rock.
3. Secondary succession is generally slower than primary succession.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Secondary succession starts where soil already exists (after a fire or abandoned farmland), so it is faster than primary succession.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Methane has a higher 100-year global warming potential than carbon dioxide.
2. Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas.
3. Water vapour is a greenhouse gas.
4. Sulphate aerosols have a net warming effect on the climate.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1–3 are correct. Sulphate aerosols reflect sunlight and help cloud formation, so their net effect is cooling, not warming.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Coral bleaching occurs when corals under thermal stress expel the symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) living in their tissues.
Statement-II: Reef-building corals are found mostly in cold, deep waters of high latitudes.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct. Reef-building corals need warm, shallow, clear tropical waters (roughly 20–30 °C), so Statement-II is wrong.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (inscription : ruler associated):
1. Hathigumpha inscription : Kharavela
2. Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar) : Samudragupta
3. Aihole inscription : Pulakeshin II
4. Junagadh inscription : Harshavardhana
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pairs 1–3 are correct (the Aihole inscription was composed by Ravikirti for Pulakeshin II). The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription is that of the Shaka ruler Rudradaman I.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Jainism:
1. Mahavira is regarded as the twenty-fourth Tirthankara.
2. Jainism does not accept the authority of the Vedas.
3. Mahavira preached in Sanskrit.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Mahavira preached in Ardhamagadhi, a Prakrit, not in Sanskrit.

questions.question: In the Delhi Sultanate, the term 'iqta' referred to:
options: Akbar's system of measuring land for revenue
A tax on the use of canal water
An assignment of the revenue of a territory to an officer in lieu of salary
questions.explanation: An iqta was a revenue assignment held by an iqtadar in return for military and administrative service. Jizya was the tax on non-Muslims, and zabt was Akbar's land-measurement system.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara Empire:
1. It was founded by Harihara and Bukka in the fourteenth century.
2. Its power declined after the Battle of Talikota in 1565.
3. Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Sangama dynasty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (founded c. 1336; Talikota 1565). Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.

questions.question: Annie Besant, the first woman to preside over the Indian National Congress, presided over which session?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of 1917. Kanpur 1925 was presided over by Sarojini Naidu, the first Indian woman president; Belgaum 1924 by Gandhi; Lucknow 1916 by A.C. Majumdar.

questions.question:
With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, consider the following statements:
1. It introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
2. Following these reforms, Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
3. It introduced a bicameral legislature at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Morley–Minto reforms introduced separate electorates, and S.P. Sinha joined the Viceroy's Executive Council as Law Member. A bicameral central legislature came only with the Government of India Act, 1919.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (Governor-General/Viceroy : associated measure):
1. Lord Dalhousie : Doctrine of Lapse
2. Lord Wellesley : Subsidiary Alliance
3. Lord Ripon : Ilbert Bill
4. Lord Curzon : Vernacular Press Act
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pairs 1–3 are correct. The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was passed under Lord Lytton; Curzon is associated with the Partition of Bengal (1905).

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (organisation : founder):
1. Servants of India Society : Gopal Krishna Gokhale
2. Satyashodhak Samaj : Jyotirao Phule
3. Self-Respect Movement : E.V. Ramasamy
4. Prarthana Samaj : Atmaram Pandurang
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All four are correct: Gokhale (1905), Phule (1873), E.V. Ramasamy 'Periyar' (1925) and Atmaram Pandurang (1867, with the support of Keshab Chandra Sen).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922.
Statement-II: At Chauri Chaura, a crowd set fire to a police station, killing the policemen inside.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both are correct, and Gandhi called off the movement precisely because the Chauri Chaura violence (5 February 1922) showed that the movement was turning violent.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (painting tradition : State):
1. Madhubani : Bihar
2. Pattachitra : Odisha
3. Warli : Gujarat
4. Kalamkari : Assam
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Madhubani (Bihar) and Pattachitra (Odisha) are correct. Warli is a tribal art of Maharashtra, and Kalamkari is associated with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nagara-style temples generally have a curvilinear shikhara over the sanctum.
2. The Vesara style combines features of the Nagara and Dravida styles.
3. The Khajuraho temples are built in the Dravida style.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Khajuraho temples (Chandelas) are classic Nagara temples.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Sufism in India:
1. The Chishti order was established in India by Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti.
2. Nizamuddin Auliya belonged to the Suhrawardi order.
3. Sama (devotional music) was an important practice of the Chishtis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Nizamuddin Auliya was a Chishti saint of Delhi, not a Suhrawardi.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Gandhara school of sculpture shows strong Greco-Roman influence.
2. The Mathura school mainly used spotted red sandstone.
3. The Amaravati school flourished in the Krishna valley under the Satavahanas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct: Gandhara art is Indo-Greek in style, Mathura sculptures are typically in spotted red sandstone, and the Amaravati school developed in the lower Krishna valley under Satavahana patronage.

questions.question:
Which of the following are tributaries of the Godavari?
1. Indravati
2. Pranhita
3. Manjira
4. Bhima
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Indravati, Pranhita and Manjira join the Godavari. The Bhima is a tributary of the Krishna.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive very heavy rainfall during the south-west monsoon.
Statement-II: The funnel-shaped valleys and steep south-facing slopes of the Khasi Hills force moist Bay of Bengal winds to rise sharply.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both are correct, and II explains I: the forced ascent of moisture-laden Bay of Bengal winds over the Khasi Hills gives intense orographic rainfall.

questions.question:
Consider the following countries:
1. Armenia
2. Azerbaijan
3. Kazakhstan
4. Turkmenistan
5. Uzbekistan
How many of the above countries border the Caspian Sea?
questions.explanation: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan border the Caspian Sea (with Russia and Iran). Armenia and Uzbekistan do not.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Laterite soils develop under high temperature and heavy rainfall with intense leaching.
2. Laterite soils are rich in oxides of iron and aluminium.
3. Khadar alluvium is older than Bhangar alluvium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Khadar is the newer alluvium of the flood plains; Bhangar is the older alluvium.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about tropical cyclones:
1. They do not form very close to the Equator because the Coriolis force is negligible there.
2. They draw their energy from the latent heat released by condensation.
3. In the Northern Hemisphere they rotate clockwise.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Northern Hemisphere cyclones rotate anticlockwise.

questions.question: Which one of the following States does NOT share a border with Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram border Bangladesh. Manipur borders Myanmar, not Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a characteristic of an El Niño event?
options: Strengthening of the easterly trade winds across the Pacific
Increased upwelling of cold water off the coast of Peru
Cooling of the eastern Pacific accompanied by heavy rain over Indonesia
Unusual warming of sea-surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific
questions.explanation: El Niño is the warm phase: trade winds weaken, upwelling off Peru decreases and the central–eastern Pacific warms. The other options describe La Niña-type conditions.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Monoclonal antibodies are produced from a single clone of cells, such as a hybridoma.
2. Gene therapy aims to treat a disease by correcting or replacing a defective gene.
3. All vaccines contain live but weakened pathogens.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Many vaccines are inactivated, subunit, toxoid or mRNA vaccines and contain no live pathogen.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Bt cotton is resistant to attack by bollworms.
Statement-II: Bt cotton carries a gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis that produces a protein toxic to certain insect larvae.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both are correct and II explains I: the Cry protein made by the inserted Bt gene kills bollworm larvae that feed on the plant.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The PSLV is mainly used to place satellites in Sun-synchronous polar orbits.
2. The LVM3 (earlier GSLV Mk III) uses an indigenously developed cryogenic upper stage.
3. In the Chandrayaan-3 mission, the lander was named Vikram and the rover Pragyan.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The LVM3 uses the indigenous C25 cryogenic stage, and Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023.

questions.question:
With reference to the NISAR satellite, consider the following statements:
1. It is a joint Earth-observation mission of NASA and ISRO.
2. It carries synthetic aperture radars operating in the L-band and the S-band.
3. It was launched on a PSLV rocket.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. NISAR was launched in July 2025 on GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota, not on a PSLV.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. A qubit can exist in a superposition of the states 0 and 1.
2. Quantum entanglement allows information to be sent faster than light.
3. Silicon is the most widely used semiconductor material in integrated circuits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Entanglement produces correlations, but it cannot transmit information faster than light (the no-communication theorem).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using renewable electricity.
2. Grey hydrogen is produced from natural gas without capturing the carbon dioxide released.
3. Burning hydrogen in air releases carbon dioxide.
4. Blue hydrogen is made from fossil fuels with carbon capture and storage.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Hydrogen burns to form water; it releases no carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which one of the following is based on total internal reflection of light?
options: Blue colour of the clear sky
Transmission of signals through optical fibres
questions.explanation: Optical fibres guide light by repeated total internal reflection at the core–cladding boundary. The blue sky is due to scattering, twinkling to atmospheric refraction, and shadows to rectilinear propagation.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the World Trade Organization (WTO):
1. It succeeded the GATT as the organisation governing world trade in 1995.
2. Its decisions are generally taken by consensus.
3. The Ministerial Conference is its highest decision-making body.
4. India is a founding member of the WTO.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995; it normally decides by consensus; the Ministerial Conference is its top body; and India has been a member since its founding (and was a GATT contracting party from 1948).

questions.question:
Consider the following countries:
1. Bangladesh
2. Myanmar
3. Nepal
4. Maldives
5. Thailand
How many of the above are members of BIMSTEC?
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC has seven members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. The Maldives is not a member, so four of the listed countries are members.

questions.question: Which one of the following countries is NOT a member of BRICS?
questions.explanation: Egypt and Ethiopia joined BRICS in 2024 and Indonesia in January 2025. Argentina was invited in 2023 but declined to join.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB):
1. Its headquarters is in Beijing.
2. India is its second-largest shareholder.
3. The United States is one of its founding members.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; China is the largest shareholder and India the second-largest. The United States is not a member of the AIIB.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The International Atomic Energy Agency reports to both the UN General Assembly and the UN Security Council.
Statement-II: The International Atomic Energy Agency is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct. The IAEA is an autonomous organisation related to the UN through a special agreement; it is not a UN specialised agency, so Statement-II is wrong.

questions.question:
With reference to Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), consider the following statements:
1. It provides health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
2. Since 2024, all senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible irrespective of income.
3. It is a Central Sector Scheme fully funded by the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the extension to everyone aged 70+ was approved in 2024. PM-JAY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with costs shared between the Centre and States, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question:
With reference to PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to install rooftop solar systems in one crore households.
2. It aims to provide up to 300 units of free electricity per month to the beneficiary households.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Power.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (scheme approved in February 2024). The nodal ministry is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, not the Ministry of Power.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs (report : publisher):
1. World Economic Outlook : International Monetary Fund
2. Global Gender Gap Report : World Economic Forum
3. Human Development Report : World Bank
4. World Investment Report : UNCTAD
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Human Development Report is published by the UNDP.

questions.question: The Global Hunger Index is published by:
questions.explanation: The Global Hunger Index is a peer-reviewed annual report published jointly by the NGOs Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe.
